sentences.text: The petitioner is also seeking inquiry in this matter and strict action against the wrong doers.
[2] According to the petitioner, respondent No.1 to 4 initiated the land acquisition proceeding on 12.09.2013 to acquire the land of area 432.347 Hectare to construct Mohanpura Dam.
Thereafter process was initiated for acquisition of additional land measuring 1015.767 Hectare under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
In total 1246.037 Hectare land of nine villages were acquired.
According to the petitioners the land bearing Survey No.250 was a Government land and the same was given on lease to one Motilal vide order dated 07.04.1984.
[3] Later on the ownership rights were also given to him as reflected in Khasra P/2 till 2009.

On 08.06.2010 and 09.06.2010, the father of respondent No.5 and 6 Late Jamnalal purchased the land bearing Survey No.250/1/3 measuring 2.0 hectare,
Survey No.250/1/5 measuring 2.0 hectare and Survey No.264/1/1 measuring 2.0 hectare total 6 hectares.
Respondent No.6 purchased, Survey No.263/1/2 measuring 2.0 hectare, Survey No.264/1/4 measuring 2.0 hectare, total 4 hectares.
Respondent No.5 purchased the land, Survey No.264/1/4 measuring 2.0 hectare and Survey No.250/1/2 measuring 2.0 hectare total 4 hectares.

[4] According to the petitioner, Late Jamnalal purchased the land from illiterate farmers without complying the provisions of Section 165(6), 165(7-b) of Madhya Pradesh Land Revenue Code, 1959 hence, such sale-deeds are void.

The father of the petitioner Motilal and other land owner filed an appeal before the SDM Rajgarh on the ground that they are illiterate person and they took loan from Jamnalal in the year 2010 and signed the mortgaged documents in order to secure the loan but he got registered a sale-deed in his name.
Initially, the SDO granted the interim relief in favour of the Motilal and others.
Meanwhile, the amount of compensation was disbursed to the Jamnalal.
Appeal filed by the Motilal was dismissed by SDO vide order dated 13.05.2016 on the ground of delay.

[5] The Motilal filed an appeal before the Commissioner on 30.05.2016 and during pendency of appeal the Munnalal died on 13.08.2017 and the appeal has been dismissed as his counsel pleaded no instruction.

According to the petitioners they had no knowledge about the aforesaid pending proceedings but after the death of Motilal they found certain papers in the house and made a complaint to the C.M. Helpline.
They applied for certified copy of the documents and the orders passed by the Revenue Authorities and filed this present petition challenging the award and claiming other reliefs.
Heard.
[6] So far as challenging the validity of the award passed in the year 2014-15 is concerned, this petition is hopelessly time barred.
The compensation was disbursed to the land owners after verification of the revenue records.
No objections were raised at the time of passing award.

After the death of Motilal, name of his son Mahesh was mutated in the revenue record on 16.10.2010, against which the Late Motilal preferred an appeal before the SDO which was dismissed on the ground of delay.

In the appeal, the case of Late Motilal was that the Jamnalal got executed the sale-deed by way of forgery, therefore, he continues to be the owner of the land and without his knowledge the name of Jamnalal has wrongly been mutated hence, it is the case of the petitioners that Jamnalal became the owner by way of registered sale-deeds.

[7] The revenue authorities are not competent to Kailash Dangi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114736963/
3 decide the validity of the sale-deed or declare the sale-deed as void

sentences.text: , Late Motilal was only challenging the mutation in the name of Mahesh Prasad or Jamnalal without challenging the sale-deeds.
After dismissal of the appeal by the SDO, an appeal was preferred before the Commissioner by Motilal.
The Motilal died on 13.08.2017 and the counsel appearing for the Motilal did not press the application as he might not have any knowledge about the legal heirs of Motilal.
These petitioners have started making complaint in the C.M. Helpline which is not a statutory authority.

[8] If the petitioners are claiming themselves to be legal heir then they should have availed the remedy to challenge the sale-deeds or apply for restoration of the appeal filed by Late Motilal before the Commissioner which was dismissed on 15.11.2017.
There are disputed question of facts involved, therefore, writ petition is not maintainable for want of alternate remedies.
In view of the above, Writ Petition is dismissed as not maintainable.

(VIVEK RUSIA) JUDGE Divyansh Kailash Dangi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114736963/
